title: Graph attention framework for site-selectivity prediction in undirected C(sp3)–H borylation

While site-selectivity prediction is established for C(sp 2 )–H borylation, significantly more challenging C(sp 3 )–H borylations remain largely unexplored. In sharp contrast, we have developed a graph-attention deep-learning framework combining molecular representations with quantum-mechanical descriptors to predict relative C(sp 3 )–H borylation site selectivities.

title: Atomic-scale structure of static screening in noble-metal nanoparticles from clusters to the conductor limit
abstractExcerpt: The static screening response of a metallic nanoparticle is encoded in its induced charge density. Integrated observables such as the dipole moment or the polarizability do not determine this density, because many different screening profiles yield the same integrals. We show that in noble-metal nanoparticles the screening charge is atomically structured, with facet, edge, and vertex sites responding differently from a smooth classical conductor.

abstractExcerpt: CD70 is well-recognized as a promising “pan-cancer” chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell target. Prior work has shown that a “natural ligand” (NL)-based CAR targeting CD70, employing its physiological interaction partner CD27, may have therapeutic advantages over antibody- based CARs. Yet while antibody-based CARs are routinely optimized by affinity maturation of their scFv, whether the binding sequence of an NL CAR can be engineered to improve its function remains unexplored.

title: Utility of Control: Scanning Probe Microscopy as a Testbed for Tool Creation in Autonomous Experimental Science
abstractExcerpt: The central task of physical characterization tools is to render unknown physical environments observable and explorable. Traditionally, progress in this field has been framed in terms of the physical instrumentation, including novel modalities, better probes, detectors, and electronics, stability, resolution, and sensitivity. However, there is an equally important control problem: how the instrument should act, at what time scale, and with what level of complexity to extract useful scientific information.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Comparative Selection Analysis of a Chemically Diverse Peptide-like DNA-Encoded Library
abstractExcerpt: DNA-encoded chemical library technology offers a cost-effective method for screening billions of compounds in a single experiment. However, achieving broad coverage of lead-like chemical space remains challenging. Here, we describe an in silico-guided strategy for the design and synthesis of a three-cycle, peptide-like DECL comprising 403,200 compounds. A chemical space model based on 4,774 commercially available amino acid building blocks was used to identify amino acids underrepresented in the original design, in order to expand the library’s physicochemical diversity.

title: Folding and Function as Two Sides of One Coin: Statistical Mechanics, Information Theory, and Deep Learning of Binding, Catalysis, and Allostery in an Exactly Enumerable Lattice Protein
abstractExcerpt: Folding and function depend on the same conformational ensemble, but they need not favor the same population distribution. We examine this relationship in a 27-residue lattice protein with 103,346 exactly enumerated compact conformations, combining statistical mechanics, information-theoretic analysis, and variational autoencoders. Exact identities separate binding into native-site recognition and population terms, distinguish transition-state complementarity from reorganization in catalysis, and express allosteric coupling as a conformational covariance.

title: Machine Learned Interatomic Forces as Inference-Time Physical Guidance for All-Atom Diffusion Peptide Design
abstractExcerpt: Diffusion-based biomolecular generative models can efficiently explore peptidereceptor sequence-structure space, but the learned generative distribution does not explicitly represent the underlying atomistic potential-energy landscape. As a result, generated complexes may contain locally unfavorable atomic arrangements even when they remain plausible under the learned structural prior.

title: Stability-Aware Structural Cleaning of Metal–Organic Frameworks for Reliable Molecular Simulation and High-Throughput Screening
abstractExcerpt: Activation of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), which involves the removal of residual solvent species, is a crucial process in converting a raw MOF structure into a computation-ready structure. The pore channels can be altered by residual solvent molecules, which in turn substantially affects the adsorption performance of MOFs. In addition, the risk that solvent removal may lead to framework collapse should not be overlooked.

abstractExcerpt: Durability of polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a major challenge, as progressive membrane aging alters proton transport and amplifies performance losses at the cell level. abstractExcerpt: Peptides occupy a particularly challenging regime of biomolecular dynamics. Short peptides lack a stable folded core and populate broad conformational ensembles, while cyclization adds ring closure, non-local residue coupling, and stereochemical diversity. Deep generative models have made remarkable progress in emulating molecular-dynamics trajectories directly, yet each is trained on windows cut at a fixed interval and therefore observes the process at a fixed temporal resolution.

title: Computational Determination of Optimal Growth Protocols for Metastable Polymorphs
abstractExcerpt: The reliable growth of a desired target structure remains a central challenge for organic-inorganic interfaces. Specific interface structures can exhibit properties that are superior compared to those of other possible interface structures, but identifying growth conditions that selectively produce a given surface structure is difficult, particularly when the target structure is thermodynamically metastable. Here, we demonstrate how time-dependent temperature and pressure protocols can be optimized to promote the high-yield formation of a metastable surface polymorph.

title: The coefficient map, not the basis, limits how machine-learning surrogates of metal–organic framework water-adsorption beds transfer to unseen materials
abstractExcerpt: Machine-learning surrogates could let designers of metal–organic framework (MOF) water harvesters screen many candidate adsorbents without solving the transport equations for each. A surrogate fails on an unseen material for one of two reasons: its reduced basis cannot represent the true field, or its map from material parameters to basis coefficients predicts the wrong coefficients. Which one limits accuracy decides where method development should go, yet it is rarely measured.

Nevertheless, a systematic comparison of catalytic behavior and pollutant removal performance between PMS and PDS over biochar is still lacking, which greatly restricts the further optimization of biochar catalyst design and operational parameters in relevant persulfate activation systems.

abstractExcerpt: Focused ion beam (FIB)-milling has been adapted to thin frozen cells for visualization of macromolecular structures in situ with cryogenic electron microscopy.
